nodes.description: A heterozygous germline SNRPE variant alters SmE, a core Sm protein of the spliceosomal U snRNPs. The start-codon variant c.1A>G and the Sm-motif missense variant p.Gly45Ser are the variants with functional data. Evidence is from human genetics (linkage, segregation, de novo occurrence).

nodes.description: Hair follicles produce too little or no hair, most consistently at the eyebrows and eyelashes, while skin, nails, teeth and sweating are spared. SmE is present in the nuclei of all hair follicle, epidermal and dermal cells of human scalp, so the restriction is not explained by expression. Whether the follicle defect is a subtle splicing change, reduced SmE dosage, or a U7 snRNP (histone mRNA 3' end processing) defect has not been tested in hair follicle cells. Evidence is human clinical phenotype plus human scalp immunohistochemistry.

nodes.description: In transfected HEK293T cells both disease variants lowered the amount of soluble SmE: c.1A>G gave full-length protein from the GTG codon at lower levels plus a mostly insoluble N-terminally truncated form, and p.Gly45Ser was incorporated into the Sm core less efficiently. The authors proposed that the variants act by reducing the soluble fraction available to U snRNPs. In lymphocytes from a c.1A>G carrier, full-length SmE was incorporated into the Sm core with near-normal efficiency, so the reduction has not been shown in patient cells. Evidence is in vitro (HEK293T overexpression, patient lymphoblastoid cells).
